anya: FYI I ran the week-long trace replay with the new queue-rationing heuristic enabled. saw an unexpected tail spike in p95 for generation requests.
kevin: what magnitude? :thinking_face:
anya: short summary from the replay output: p50 roughly unchanged, p95 jumped from ~210ms to ~320ms using the same knobs.
replay-bot: replay run 2201234567 completed
replay-bot: config: queue_rationer=v2, token_budget_target=256, kv_prefetch=on, kernel_mode=auto
replay-bot: aggregate: p50=48ms p95=320ms cpu_ms/op=12.3 gpu_ms/op=9.8 dropped_batches=0 abandoned_batches=27
raj: abandoned_batches 27 is alarming 14 where are those coming from? baseline had 0.
lina: grabbed a flamegraph from one of the hot workers 14 looks like extra time spent during kernel fallback when batches are small. profiler excerpt:
```:
small-batch path: kernel_select() -> try_vec_kernel() failed -> fallback_generic() + cache_lock wait
avg extra = ~85ms on p95 traces
```
kevin: so kernel fallback latency + KV cache lock contention when rationer chops queues smaller? that fits the p95 regression.
anya: exact issue: queue_rationer slices large request queues to improve fairness, which increases frequency of small-batch executions and triggers the vec-kernel probe more often.
devex: can we bias kernel_select to avoid probing vec kernels for very short sequences? we used to have a min_seq threshold.
lina: there is a threshold, but with rationer the effective seq length distribution shifts down. current logic probes when batch_tokens < probe_threshold && model.supports_vec. our classifier is misclassifying many short batches as "try-vec".
kevin: action plan (quick): 1) reduce token_budget_target in experiment arm to reduce small-slab churn; 2) add a conservative override: skip vec probe if estimated probe cost > kernel_probe_cost_threshold and use generic kernel.
anya: proposed replay A/B: control = queue_rationer=v1 token_budget=256; experiment = queue_rationer=v2 token_budget=192 + kernel_probe_cost_threshold=40ms. measure p50/p95, abandoned_batches, kernel_probe_rate.
ops-bot: scheduled replay job: replay-a-b-2201234567 at 2201234590 (queued)
raj: also add per-trace stratification: heavy-KV traces vs light-KV traces. kv_prefetch interacts heavily with fallback behavior.
lina: i'll attach a small trace snippet showing the hit pattern (will post link). local re-run command for reproducing the flame output:
```:bash
./replay --trace traces/2026-03-10/trace-9812.json \
  --config queue_rationer=v2 token_budget=192 kernel_probe_threshold=40 \
  --profile --emit-flame
```
anya: once replay finishes let's inspect new metrics: "vec_probe_success_rate" and "vec_probe_failure_latency". if failure latency keeps dominating, bias kernel selection further for batches < 8 tokens.
devex: i'll wire up the A/B harness to auto-plot kernel_probe_rate vs p95 and add an alert if abandoned_batches > 5% of total.
kevin: also add a runtime guard: if abandoned_batches > 10 in a 60s window, disable rationer locally and fall back to v1 so customer traffic isn't impacted.
anya: i'll run the replays and follow up with results + a small kernel_select patch. tagging @devex @lina @raj for canary.
lina: i'll open a PR to expose kernel_probe_threshold as a runtime flag and skip vec probe for batch_len < 8. will keep it minimal.
raj: logging action items:
- anya: run replays and post results (due: +2h)
- devex: A/B plots + alert (due: +4h)
- lina: PR for kernel_probe_threshold and short-batch override (due: +6h)
- kevin: runtime guard for auto-disable rationer (due: +8h)
